newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes just easier on light selling.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes just easier on light selling.

text.p: Precious metals markets opened quietly and little changed in Europe on Monday following an unspectacular end to last week in New York.
Dealers said there were few if any incentives for speculators to buy gold at present.
"If the price does not have the aspiration to go up, there is no incentive for a speculator to buy gold," one dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $354.20 per ounce versus $355.75 on Friday afternoon when the market was at the top of a brief short-covering rally.
There was little guidance from gold from the Far East.
Light selling came into Hong Kong which some dealers attributed to Australian producer activity while others maintained the selling was from weak professional longs.
Either way it capped any nascent move firmer.
"There was a bit of light selling (in Europe) this morning which took it below $355.00," one dealer said, while another noted gold was still a $352-$355 market.
Concerns about central bank selling continued to dominate the market outlook following the announcement last Monday that the Dutch central bank had sold 300 tonnes of gold.
"The market is typified by nervousness," one dealer said.
He added that any moves higher in the past week had been related to profit taking on short sales rather than any fresh speculative buying.
"No speculators are looking at gold as an investment. It needs something to change their minds," the dealer added.
Meanwhile technical analysts said gold was seen having problems penetrating $356.00 where producer-related selling would come in.
One the downside support should be secure at $352.00 and $350.00 unless selling intensified.
The other precious metals were quiet around Friday's closing levels having been largely ignored before Europe opened.
Silver was a couple of cents easier at $4.74/$4.76but continued to give the inpression of having more upside potential than gold.
"It has held fairly well compared to gold," a dealer said.
Platinum and palladium were little changed as well and took some support from the continuing silence from Moscow on contract talks for supplying Japan with metal this year.
"There has been no sign of change there," one dealer said.
Platinum was at $359.25/$360.25 down $1.05 but palladium was up $0.95 at $121.75/$122.75.
